title: Why does an eastern gray squirrel bury nuts?
answer: An eastern gray squirrel can save food by digging a little hole and covering a nut with soil. A hiding place for food is called a cache. It may bury nuts in lots of places instead of putting them all together. When there is less food around, the squirrel can search for what it saved. It uses its memory and its sense of smell to find some of the nuts. A nut that stays in the soil may sprout instead.
facts: A gray squirrel can build a leafy nest high in a tree or use a hole in a trunk.

title: How does an eastern chipmunk carry so many seeds?
answer: A chipmunk has a cheek pouch on each side of its mouth that can stretch. The pouches hold several small seeds to the sides until it can put them down. When it reaches its burrow, the chipmunk can drop the seeds into a storage space. Then it can go out for another load. In cold weather, a chipmunk can wake up from periods of deep rest and eat from what it stored.
facts: An eastern chipmunk’s burrow can have separate places for sleeping and storing food.

Which small bird remembers places where it hides food?

title: Why does a white-tailed deer lift its tail when it runs?
answer: A white-tailed deer’s tail blends in with its coat when the tail hangs down. If the deer is alarmed, it can lift the tail and show the bright white fur underneath. It may hold the tail up as it bounds away. The flash is easy to see among the trees and can signal danger to other deer. Deer often use places where woods and open land meet.
facts: The spots on a young white-tailed deer can help it blend in with patches of light and shade.

How can wildlife cross a human road?

title: How does a raccoon use its front paws?
answer: A raccoon has five long toes on each front paw. It can use the toes to turn food around, feel along the ground, and pick up small things. The paws are sensitive to touch, which helps when a raccoon searches under leaves or in shallow water. A raccoon may handle food in water, but it can also find and eat its meal on dry ground. Many raccoons look for food after dark.
facts: Raccoons eat many kinds of foods, including fruit, insects, and animals they find in shallow water.

title: Why does a Virginia opossum carry babies in a pouch?
answer: A Virginia opossum gives birth to very small young that still need a protected place to grow. The babies crawl into a pouch on their mother’s belly. There they drink milk while they grow bigger. Later, young opossums can ride on their mother’s back as she moves about. An opossum is a marsupial, which means it belongs to a group of mammals whose young are born at a very early stage of development and keep growing while they nurse.
facts: When frightened, a Virginia opossum can go still and look as if it is dead.

title: Where does a groundhog spend the winter?
answer: A groundhog, also called a woodchuck, spends the coldest part of the year inside a burrow. It goes into hibernation, when its body cools and its heartbeat and breathing slow down. It uses energy stored as fat from the food it ate before winter. In warmer months, a burrow also offers a groundhog a place to rest and hide. It can have more than one entrance.
facts: A groundhog belongs to the squirrel family, but it spends more of its time on the ground than an eastern gray squirrel.

title: How does an eastern cottontail stay close to cover?
answer: An eastern cottontail often feeds on grass or low plants near a tangle of bushes. If something startles it, the rabbit can bolt into thick cover where a larger animal may have trouble following. The rabbit’s brownish back helps it blend into leaves and dry grass while it sits still. Its little tail has a white underside that can flash as it runs away. That fluffy white patch gives cottontails their name.
facts: A cottontail often feeds around dawn or dusk, though it may come out at other times.

title: How does a striped skunk give a warning?
answer: A striped skunk often tries to make a threat back away before using its strong-smelling spray. It can stamp its front feet and lift its tail. If it needs to defend itself, it can direct a spray from glands below the tail. The skunk’s black-and-white coat stands out even in dim light. An animal that has met a skunk before may recognize its pattern and keep its distance.
facts: The shape and width of the white stripes can differ from one striped skunk to another.

What color helps a cottontail blend into leaves?

title: How does a red fox catch prey it cannot see?
answer: A mouse can move under grass or snow without showing itself. A red fox may stop, tilt its head, and listen. Its ears can pick up small sounds that suggest where the animal is moving. The fox can leap into the air and come down with its front paws near the spot it heard. Foxes also eat things they do not have to pounce on, including fruit and insects.
facts: A red fox’s bushy tail often has a white tip.

title: How does a chickadee save food for later?
answer: A black-capped chickadee can take one seed and fly off to tuck it away in a small hiding place. It may hide food in many separate spots, such as cracks in bark. Later it can remember where each food cache is and go back when it needs a meal. The bird is small but can stay through the winter in much of its range. It eats insects as well as seeds and other plant food.
facts: A black-capped chickadee can hide a food item in a different spot from the one it used for its last item.

title: Why does a northern cardinal have a thick bill?
answer: A northern cardinal uses its thick, pointed bill like a little pair of grips. It can hold a seed and crack its outer coat, then take the softer part inside. Seeds are a frequent part of its food. Cardinals also eat fruit and insects. Both males and females have a point of feathers on top of the head, though the male is usually a much brighter red.
facts: A northern cardinal can stay in the same general area through all seasons instead of making a long trip south.

title: Why does an American robin stop and look down on a lawn?
answer: An American robin searching short grass often runs a few steps, stops, and studies the ground. It can pull out an earthworm where it finds one. An open lawn gives it room to see, run, and stop. The bird does not eat only worms, though. It also eats insects and fruit. In cooler months, robins often gather with other robins in places where berries and other fruit are available.
facts: The American robin has an orange breast, but it is a different bird from the European robin.

title: How can a blue jay carry more than one acorn?
answer: A blue jay does not have to carry every acorn by the tip of its bill. It has room in its throat to hold some food while it travels. A jay can carry nuts from under an oak to another place, where it can hide them for later. Some buried nuts never get eaten. If one stays in a good patch of soil, a young oak may grow far from its parent tree.
facts: Besides acorns and other nuts, blue jays can eat seeds and small animals such as insects.

title: How can a ruby-throated hummingbird stop in midair?
answer: A ruby-throated hummingbird can beat its wings rapidly while keeping its body nearly in one spot. Its wings sweep back and forth and turn between strokes, helping the bird stay up without moving ahead. Hovering lets it put its slender bill into a flower that cannot hold its weight. The bird takes sweet nectar with its tongue. It also catches small insects and spiders for part of its food.
facts: The bright patch on an adult male’s throat can appear dark when it catches the light at a different angle.

title: Why does a downy woodpecker tap on a branch?
answer: A downy woodpecker may tap a branch to look for insects under its bark. It can also hit wood in a very quick series called a drum. The sound can tell another woodpecker that it has entered an occupied area or help birds find each other. A thin branch can hold this small bird while it searches for insects, even if that branch is too narrow for a heavier woodpecker.
facts: Downy woodpeckers are small enough to feed on some thick weed stems as well as branches.

title: What makes long holes in a tree trunk?
answer: A pileated woodpecker uses its strong bill to chip pieces of wood away. It may leave a long, roughly rectangular hole while it searches for carpenter ants and other insects in a trunk or log. Bits of wood can collect on the ground below. The hole it makes for a nest is shaped differently. The nest is up in a tree, where the birds have a sheltered place for their eggs.
facts: A pileated woodpecker is a large black bird with a red crest on top of its head.

title: Why does a wood duckling jump out of a tree?
answer: A wood duck often nests in a tree hole near water. After the eggs hatch, the ducklings can climb to the opening even though they cannot fly yet. When their mother calls from below, they jump down and follow her to water. The tree hole helps shelter eggs while the mother is sitting on them, but the ducklings leave it early so they can swim and search for food.
facts: A female wood duck can also use a wooden nest box with an opening like a tree hole.

title: Why does a mallard tip its tail into the air?
answer: A mallard can dip its head beneath the surface to reach plants or small animals. If the food is a little deeper, it may tip its whole front end down until the tail points up. This way of feeding is called dabbling. The bird can stay near the surface because it is reaching into shallow water. Other ducks can dive all the way underneath to find food.
facts: A mallard may also walk on land to feed where it finds seeds or other food.

title: Why does a great blue heron stand so still in water?
answer: A great blue heron can wade into shallow water on its long legs. It may wait with its neck bent until a fish or other small animal comes close, then quickly reach forward with its pointed bill. Standing quietly can keep the bird from warning nearby prey. A heron may also take slow steps as it hunts. The same long legs help it search without getting most of its body wet.
facts: A great blue heron can nest in the branches of a tree even though it often feeds in water.

title: How does an osprey keep hold of a slippery fish?
answer: An osprey can spot a fish near the surface while flying over water. It drops down and extends its feet to grab the fish. It can turn an outer toe backward, so two toes grip on each side. Curved claws and rough patches on the feet help it hold on. After the bird rises again, it often carries the fish head first, lined up with its own flight.
facts: Fish make up almost all of an osprey’s food.

title: How can a barred owl find food in the dark?
answer: A barred owl often hunts from a branch near a clear spot in the woods. It can listen for a small animal moving in the leaves and use its large eyes when there is some light. Soft edges on owl wing feathers can help make flight quieter. From the branch, the owl can drop toward the sound. A barred owl may also call after dark with a series of hoots.
facts: People often remember one barred owl call as sounding like the words “Who cooks for you?”

title: Where does a wild turkey sleep at night?
answer: A wild turkey can spend much of a day walking on the ground. It may scratch through old leaves to find nuts, seeds, or insects. Later it can beat its broad wings and fly up to a branch to spend the night. A spot where a bird rests like this is called a roost. Sleeping above the ground can put the turkey farther from some animals that might hunt it.
facts: Wild turkeys can fly, though they usually travel short distances in the air rather than making long flights.

title: Why does a painted turtle sit on a log in the sun?
answer: A painted turtle gets much of its body heat from the world around it. On a sunny day it can climb onto a log and warm up. Spending time in the sun this way is called basking. More than one turtle may use the same good spot. If something startles them, the turtles can slide off the log into the water, where they are quick swimmers.
facts: Painted turtles have colorful stripes on their skin and often red marks along part of the shell.

title: Why can’t a snapping turtle hide completely in its shell?
answer: A common snapping turtle has a broad shell across its back, but only a small hard area under its body. It cannot tuck all of its head, legs, and tail between those two parts as some other turtles can. In water, a snapping turtle may simply swim or walk away from a disturbance. On land it may defend itself quickly with its strong jaws if it feels trapped.
facts: A snapping turtle has a long tail with raised bumps along the top.

title: Why does a garter snake flick its tongue?
answer: A common garter snake can pick up tiny traces from the air or ground with its tongue. When the tongue comes back inside, the snake brings those traces to a sensing area in its mouth. This helps it find nearby animals or follow a scent left by another snake. The two tips of the tongue can sample slightly different spots. A quick flick is a way of gathering information about its surroundings.
facts: Common garter snakes can eat several kinds of small animals, including frogs and earthworms.

title: Why do such small frogs make such loud peeps?
answer: A male spring peeper sends out a high call that can sound like a clear whistle. A pouch of skin under its throat, called a vocal sac, puffs up with air as it calls. The sound can help a female find the calling frog among plants at the edge of the water. When lots of male peepers call close together, it can be hard to pick out just one voice.
facts: Many spring peepers have a dark mark shaped like an X on the back.

title: How does a wood frog survive part of its body freezing?
answer: A wood frog can spend the winter under leaves near the ground. As its surroundings get cold, some water outside its cells can turn to ice. Its body can send extra sugar to its tissues, which helps protect its cells. The frog’s breathing and heartbeat can stop for a time. If conditions stay within what the frog can survive, it can begin moving again after it thaws.
facts: A wood frog has a dark patch that runs through each eye and can look like part of a mask.

title: Why does an American bullfrog make a low booming call?
answer: A male American bullfrog makes a deep call that can carry across a pond. It pushes air through the sound-making parts of its throat. A vocal sac, or pouch under the lower jaw, can swell and help the call carry. Other bullfrogs can hear it from a distance, which helps them find one another or learn where another male is calling. The calls are especially common in the warmer months.
facts: An American bullfrog is much larger than a spring peeper.

title: Why do American toad eggs look like long strings?
answer: A female American toad can lay many small dark eggs in a long string of clear jelly. The string can settle among plants in shallow water. The eggs hatch into tadpoles that swim and feed in the water. As they grow, they develop legs and their tails shrink. The little toads can leave the water after they have changed enough to live on land.
facts: Adult American toads have bumpy skin and can live in woods, fields, and gardens.

title: How can a red-backed salamander breathe without lungs?
answer: An eastern red-backed salamander has no lungs. Oxygen can pass into its body across its moist skin and the lining of its mouth. When the ground gets dry, the salamander may hide beneath a damp log or stone. Unlike many salamanders, this kind does not need a pond for its young to swim in. Its eggs can hatch into tiny land-living salamanders in a moist hiding place.
facts: Some eastern red-backed salamanders lack the red stripe that gives the species its name.

title: Where does a dragonfly live before it can fly?
answer: A young dragonfly lives underwater. In this stage it is called an aquatic nymph. It has no working wings yet and can catch other small animals that pass nearby. Some kinds stay underwater for months or longer. When a nymph is ready to become a flying adult, it can climb out on a plant stem. The adult then pulls free from its old skin and opens its new wings.
facts: You may find an empty dragonfly skin clinging to a stem near the water.

title: How can you tell a damselfly from a dragonfly?
answer: A resting damselfly usually holds its four wings together above or along its body. Many dragonflies rest with theirs pointing out to the sides. A damselfly usually has a thin body and eyes that look widely spaced. These clues work for many kinds, but not for all of them. Some damselflies, for instance, can rest with their wings partly open. Both kinds of insect begin life in water.
facts: The front and back wings of a damselfly are usually more similar in shape than the front and back wings of a dragonfly.

title: Why do some fireflies flash in patterns?
answer: Some fireflies make short flashes using a light-making part of the body. The number of flashes and the space between them can form a pattern. Other fireflies of the same species may answer that pattern with their own light. This helps some males and females find one another after dark. Not every kind of firefly makes the same signal, and some adult fireflies do not flash at all.
facts: In a few kinds of firefly, many males can flash at nearly the same time.

title: Why does a bumblebee buzz while holding a flower?
answer: Some flowers hold pollen inside parts that have tiny openings. A bumblebee can grip the flower and shake it with the muscles it uses for flight. Its wings do not have to flap during this buzz. The shake can loosen the pollen so it falls onto the bee. Some pollen may travel to another flower later. This behavior is called buzz pollination, and it helps flowers such as tomatoes release pollen.
facts: A bumblebee also makes a different buzzing sound while it flies.

title: Why does a leafcutter bee cut neat circles from leaves?
answer: A leafcutter bee can use its mouth parts to snip a small, rounded piece from a leaf. The bee carries the piece away rather than eating it. It can fit several pieces together to line tiny rooms in a hollow stem or other narrow opening. In a room it leaves food and an egg. The young bee has its own protected space and a supply of food as it grows.
facts: The bee can leave nearly round or oval openings along the edge of a leaf.

title: What is a lady beetle looking for on a plant?
answer: Many lady beetles feed on tiny insects called aphids. Aphids often gather on stems or beneath leaves where they can take in plant juices. A lady beetle can crawl along those parts of the plant searching for a meal. Its young can eat aphids too, even though they do not look like the round adult beetles. A growing lady beetle changes shape before it becomes an adult.
facts: Different kinds of lady beetles have different spot patterns, and some do not have spots.

title: How can a water strider stand on water?
answer: Water molecules attract one another. At the surface, that attraction makes it harder for something to break through, a property called surface tension. The long legs of a water strider spread its weight across the surface. Tiny hairs on the legs help keep them from getting wet. An insect can press tiny dimples into the water and still stay on top as it pushes itself forward.
facts: Water striders can use their legs to sense small waves made by prey near the surface.

title: Why do some young caddisflies carry cases made of stones?
answer: Some young caddisflies build a small tube around their soft bodies. They use silk to hold together bits of sand, tiny stones, or pieces of stems found nearby. The caddisfly case protects the body as the insect drags it along while it crawls on the bottom. If it is disturbed, it may pull its head and front legs inside. Other kinds of young caddisflies make shelters that stay in one place.
facts: Some caddisflies use silk to make nets that catch food drifting past instead of carrying a case.

title: Why do brook trout need cool water?
answer: Brook trout often live in cold, clear streams. Cold water can hold more dissolved oxygen than warm water. Brook trout use their gills to take in that oxygen, and they can struggle when water gets too warm. Streamside trees can shade a stretch of water, and groundwater can also help keep some streams cool. In hot weather, a cooler pool or spring-fed stretch can be especially important.
facts: A brook trout has pale markings along its back and small colored spots along its sides.

title: Why does a bluegill fan a round patch on the bottom?
answer: A male bluegill can sweep loose material aside with its tail to make a shallow, round nest on the bottom of a pond or lake. Several males may build nests close together. A female can leave eggs in a nest, and the male may guard the eggs and young fish for a time. Shallow water can make the nests easy to see from above when the water is clear.
facts: The dark patch on the side of a bluegill’s head lies at the back of its gill cover.

title: How does a chain pickerel hide while it waits for food?
answer: A chain pickerel can wait in or near water plants with most of its long body barely moving. If a small fish swims within reach, the pickerel can dart forward. Waiting near plants can help it avoid being noticed. Dark marks along its sides connect into shapes that look like a chain. You may see this pattern more easily than the fish itself when it emerges into open water.
facts: The chain pickerel and northern pike belong to the same family, but are different kinds of fish.

title: Why does an Atlantic salmon return to a river?
answer: Many Atlantic salmon begin life in fresh water. When they grow and their bodies change, they swim downstream and can spend years feeding in the ocean. Adults can return upstream to reproduce in a river, often the one they came from. Eggs develop in gravel where river water can flow around them. Not all Atlantic salmon make the ocean trip. Some populations spend their lives in fresh water.
facts: Some Atlantic salmon survive after laying or fertilizing eggs and can return to a river to reproduce again.

title: Why does an American eel head back out to sea?
answer: An American eel begins life far out in the Atlantic Ocean in a place called the Sargasso Sea. Young eels can drift toward the coast, then move into rivers or other coastal waters to grow. Some travel far inland, while others stay closer to salt water. After years of growing, adults leave those places and head out to sea to reproduce. This fish migration goes in a different direction from that of many salmon.
facts: Very young American eels are thin and nearly see-through.
